evals.prompt: Create a Base that shows all my notes tagged #project, sorted by due date, with columns for status, owner, and last modified.
evals.description: Basic Base with filter, sort, and column selection.
expected_output_criteria: Produces a valid .base file with the documented YAML / JSON-equivalent structure
Filter targets the `tag` property and matches '#project' correctly
Sort is applied to the due-date property in ascending order by default
Column / view configuration explicitly lists status, owner, last-modified
Does not invent property names; uses standard Obsidian frontmatter property syntax

evals.prompt: I want a Base with a card view of my reading list grouped by status (to-read, reading, done), filtered to books only, with a formula showing days since I added each book.
evals.description: Medium: card view, grouping, formula column.
expected_output_criteria: Selects the card view (not table) and groups by status
Filter clause restricts to books only (type or tag based, whichever the property model uses)
Formula uses the supported Bases function syntax to compute days-since-added (not free-form JavaScript)
Group order follows a sensible reading flow (e.g., reading first, then to-read, then done) or is explicitly explained
Outputs a complete .base file the user can drop in and open

evals.prompt: Refactor my existing meetings.base so each row links to its source note, filters out cancelled meetings, and adds a weekly summary row counting attendees per week.
evals.description: Hard: edit existing base, add link column, add aggregation.
expected_output_criteria: Reads the existing meetings.base before editing rather than starting from scratch
Adds a link / file-name column wired to the underlying note rather than a plain text title
Filter explicitly excludes status == cancelled (or equivalent) and does not over-filter active rows
Aggregation uses the documented summary syntax (count, group-by-week) rather than a custom formula hack
Preserves the user's existing columns and view settings except where the user asked to change them
